title: Closing Canario Terminal Source Code: A Maintainer's Perspective
summary: Raphael Amorim, an experienced open-source contributor, explains his decision to close-source Canario Terminal, a project he built for personal use. He cites the high maintenance cost of open-source projects, including spam, low-effort issues, and AI-generated pull requests, as the primary reasons. While the source code remains available in older versions for forking, Amorim emphasizes his focus on maintaining Rio, another open-source project he loves, and developing Canario at his own pace without external demands.
key_points: Raphael Amorim has a long history in open-source, starting at age 17, but has decided to close-source Canario Terminal.
The decision stems from the high cost of maintaining open-source projects, including spam, low-effort issues, and AI-generated pull requests.
Canario was built for personal use, with no commercial intent or VC funding.
The source code of older versions remains available for forking, but no further open-source contributions will be accepted.
Amorim will continue maintaining Rio, another open-source project, but will develop Canario independently without external input.
The post highlights the challenges faced by open-source maintainers, including time, energy, and the burden of community demands.
